title: Prefill prober with confidence signaling, routing heuristics, and fallback playbook
creator: Maya Rodriguez
description:
Goal: implement a lightweight prefill probing mechanism that lets the runtime opportunistically route requests to a fast-path model variant while maintaining correctness via quantitative acceptance metrics and a robust fallback playbook.

Scope:
- Prefill probe design: small, inexpensive prefill token requests (4-12 tokens) executed on candidate fast models to estimate whether fast decode will match the full-model output distribution sufficiently.
- Confidence signaling: define and emit compact metrics (probe_score, entropy_delta, top_k_overlap) used to accept/decline optimistic routing.
- Kernel and attention considerations: ensure probes pick kernel-friendly paths (quantized kernels, fused attention) and respect KV cache compatibility to avoid migration costs on fallback.
- Fallback plan: deterministic, per-session rollback with exponential backoff and circuit-breaker to limit repeated expensive fallbacks.
- Telemetry & dashboards: new events and charts for probe latency, acceptance rate, mismatch rate, rollback triggers, and per-model delta in token costs.

Non-goals: implementing any new model training or model distillation; changes to public API surface.

Success criteria (canary gate):
- Mean 95th percentile latency reduction on routed requests >= 15% vs baseline.
- Acceptance precision: >98% (fraction of probes accepted that produce acceptable downstream tokens by our acceptance tests).
- Fallback rate <= 2% for routed traffic after warm-up.
- No increase in customer-observed hallucination or regression alerts for monitored prompts during canary window.

Trade-offs & decisions so far:
- Probe length: shorter probes (4 tokens) reduce cost but lower statistical power; we favor 8 tokens as a compromise for chat+completion workloads.
- Kernel selection: fast model variants should use int8 quantized kernels with fused attention when available; however, for very long-context workloads we will prefer float16 kernels to avoid precision loss when acceptance confidence is marginal.
- Cache strategy: probes must reuse the same KV cache 'namespace' where possible; if model variants are incompatible, we detect and mark the session to preemptively avoid probe routing for subsequent requests.

Implementation plan:
1) Instrumentation: add probe events (router.prefill_probe.sent, router.prefill_probe.latency_ms, router.prefill_probe.score, router.router.decision, router.fallback.invoked).
2) Probe runner: lightweight worker in runtime that issues a small synchronous prefill to candidate models and computes probe_score = weighted(sum(softmax_topk_overlap, 1 - normalized_entropy_delta)).
3) Acceptance policy: simple threshold policy configurable per deployment tier (e.g., hosted: 0.87, dedicated: 0.80) with a pluggable policy object.
4) Fallback: immediate full decode on mismatch; per-session probation window (default 60s) where probe routing is disabled after N consecutive fallbacks; implement per-model circuit-breaker.
5) Simulation & tests: synthetic traffic generator validating acceptance precision on gold prompts; offline replay against production logs to estimate expected acceptance/fallback rate.
6) Canary rollout: stage 0 (internal), stage 1 (1% production, 24h), stage 2 (10% production, 72h), rollback if mismatch rate > 2% or latency regressions occur.

Operational alerts to add:
- probe.acceptance_rate < 80% over 10m
- probe.fallback_rate > 2% over 5m
- decoder.rollback_surge > baseline + 0.5% over 5m

Notes on evaluation: we will use multiple acceptance metrics in combination:
- top_k_overlap: Jaccard of top-5 logits between probe and full-prefill.
- entropy_delta_norm: normalized change in token probability entropy.
- token_agreement_span: fraction of first M tokens where greedy decode matches.
Thresholds, weights, and M vary by model family and customer tier; these are runtime-configurable via the router config.
